lesson: The accrual ratio is a WEAK kill criterion for payables-funded working-capital frauds: PC Jeweller's accrual ratio held at 0.02 while cumulative CFO/PAT broke to 0.34, because the inventory build is financed through trade payables (gold metal loans), which never passes through the accrual line.
action: Kill-criteria selection should weight cash-conversion and stock-flow criteria over accrual criteria when the funding channel is payables-side; consider a payables-divergence criterion (payables growth vs COGS growth) for this model.

lesson: Broadcasting the report's single confidence (0.38) as P(holds) for every criterion is miscalibrated by construction: the two cash criteria deserved a lower P(holds) than the accrual criterion on the report's own reasoning. Brier 0.224 barely beats a coin flip despite the verdict being right.
action: criteria.py should assign per-criterion probabilities (e.g. flagged-check criteria get P(holds) well below 0.5; clean-check criteria above), not one broadcast confidence. A calibration question for the golden set.

lesson: Comparative-column restatements of the CASH FLOW statement are themselves a forensic signal: the FY18 filing restated FY17 CFO from 756.48 to 794.35 (+37.87cr, +5%) and its restated FY17 CFS legs do not tie to the printed net change (794.35-530.06-47.45 != 311.74) - the V7 identity refuses the column. A company revising its cash history upward while its current cash collapses is quiet-change material (pattern P5).
evidence: AR-FY18-PCJ-AR-FY18.pdf comparative FY17 = 794.35 (registered, classified 'restated' by quarantine)
action: A deterministic restatement-log across filings (metric, period, old, new, delta) is nearly free from the quarantine's 'restated' classifications and should reach the report as its own section.

lesson: A treasury-heavy company systematically shows CFO/PAT below 1.0 without any earnings-quality problem: the indirect-method cash flow subtracts interest and dividend income from PBT in operating activities and reports it under investing. Symphony earns ~20% of PBT as treasury income on a ~Rs 422cr investment book and converts 0.55; the check reads that as a HIGH flag.
action: Do NOT move the cfo_pat threshold on one observation. The golden set should test whether cfo_pat needs an other-income adjustment (CFO vs PAT-excluding-investment-income) or whether other_income_share should modulate the flag's severity. Recorded as a calibration question, not a code change (ADR-0048).

lesson: Choosing a company to test FALSE POSITIVES found three defects in one run, where two fraud runs found none of them. A clean company with unusual-but-legitimate structure (stub period, outsourced manufacturing, treasury book) exercises paths a fraud never touches.
evidence: ADR-0048 defects 1-3, all first observed on Symphony
action: Keep alternating: the golden set should be built as matched pairs (a fraud and a clean company of the SAME business shape), not as a list of frauds.

source: first lender filing read end-to-end (FY25, ADR-0050)
lesson: A capability can be fully unit-tested, calibrated on real figures, documented as validated, selected by config — and still be unreachable from a real document. The lender path was broken in three independent places (vocabulary, shape detection, check evaluation) while quality.py's lender functions passed every test they had.
evidence: 7 lender checks with no evaluator in checks.py
VALIDATION_TIER0.md cited as proof the firm handles lenders
action: For any claimed capability, ask what a REAL DOCUMENT would have to travel through to exercise it, and test that path — not the leaf function. Candidate audit: which other checks in the playbooks have no evaluator? (contract_asset_divergent, guarantees_heavy, capitalised_cost_heavy, adjusted_ebitda_gap, revenue_inflation partially.)

lesson: A lender needs an earnings-quality measure to replace CFO/PAT, which is now suppressed because it tracks book growth. Candidates: accrual-style measures on net interest income vs credit cost, or the gap between reported PAT and (NII - opex - credit cost). Not invented here — a golden-set calibration question.
action: Add to the golden-set design: a lender pair (a clean grower and a known lender fraud) is needed to calibrate any replacement measure, since the failure mode is precisely a growing book.
